meanings.note: Imperative senti grabs a listener's attention ('listen / look').
Mi sento a casa ('I feel at home'); sentirsela (te la senti?, 'do you feel up to it?').

examples.trans: Listen, do you have a minute?

meanings.note: Movement toward the speaker or listener (vieni con me, 'come with me').

examples.trans: On Sunday I am coming too.

meanings.note: Marks accompaniment, instrument, or attitude.
Stressed pronoun after prepositions (con me) and clitic form before li/lo/la/ne (me ne danno, me li sento).

sapere.gloss: to know (a fact or how to)

meanings.note: Knowing facts or answers (sa dov'è?, non lo so).
Followed directly by an infinitive (sai giocare?, 'do you know how to play?').

examples.trans: Do you know how to play foosball?

meanings.note: Links to game and sport names with preposition a: giocare a tennis, a biliardino.
Marks destination, location in cities, or indirect recipient.
Links activities and idioms such as giocare a tennis or a presto.
Literally 'little billiards'; a classic Italian bar and break-room game.

examples.trans: There is a foosball table at the cafe.

meanings.note: Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
Literally a dragon; essere un drago means being brilliant at a game or skill.

examples.trans: At cards he is an ace!

meanings.note: Truncates to gran before many nouns (in gran forma); un grande means 'a legend'.

examples.trans: He works in a big studio.

meanings.note: Adjective from sposare ('to marry').

examples.trans: They have been married for five years.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction offering alternatives.

examples.trans: Are you married or in a relationship?

meanings.note: Covers both having a steady partner and being formally engaged.

examples.trans: Are you married or seeing someone?
She has been in a relationship for two years.

meanings.note: Conversational contrast word, slightly weightier than ma.

examples.trans: It is nice, though it costs too much.

stare.gloss: to stay; to be; to live

meanings.note: Stai fermo ('stay still'), stare in porta ('play in goal').
Come stai?, sto scherzando (stare + gerund for ongoing action), sta a Milano ('lives in Milan').

examples.trans: I am writing a note right now.

meanings.note: Question word asking manner or requesting repetition (Come, scusa?).
Introduces a comparison.
Unstressed familiar 2nd-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun.
Contact someone by voice or telephone.
With mi/ti/si, expresses someone's or something's name.
Familiar singular subject pronoun; darsi del tu means addressing each other informally.
Location or state; in silenzio means quietly, in porta means in goal.
Literally 'door'; in football and foosball, stare in porta means playing in goal.

segnare.gloss: to write down; to log; to score

meanings.note: Recording an entry in a notebook or report; in football, scoring a goal.

examples.trans: Write everything down in the notebook.

meanings.note: Contraction of preposition su + masculine singular article il (sul set, sul serio).
On a film set, il diario di lavorazione is the official daily production log.

examples.text: Segna tutto sul diario di lavorazione.
examples.trans: Log everything on the production report.

meanings.note: Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.
In cinema, diario di lavorazione is the daily production report.

examples.text: Segna tutto sul diario di lavorazione.
examples.trans: Note everything on the production log.

meanings.note: In singular, a single camera take; in plural, filming operations.
Past participle/adjective of sospendere, used in official notices (riprese sospese).
In telegraphic notes, causa + noun means 'because of / due to'.

examples.trans: Train delayed due to bad weather.

meanings.note: Literally a fishing or goal net; in broadcasting, the TV network commissioning a show.

examples.trans: The ball lands in the net.

meanings.note: Movement away from the speaker or toward a destination.
Used in expressions like va bene, ti va, or andare male.
Origin in space or time (da casa, da oggi, da capo).
Before a person's name (vai da Duccio), means going to where they are.

examples.trans: I am going over to Arianna's.

meanings.note: Links words or clauses; distinct from accented è, meaning is.
Takes a for the person asked and di before an infinitive.

examples.trans: I ask you for a favour.

meanings.note: Asks quantity or duration (quanto per Corinna?, quanto ci mette?).

examples.trans: How long does it take you?

meanings.note: Locative or idiomatic clitic, as in c'è (there is) or metterci (take time to do).
First-person plural object or reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: How long does it take him?
We will see each other soon.

mettere.gloss: to put; to place; to take (time)

meanings.note: Put something somewhere (mettere il cuore); metterci expresses how long something takes.

examples.trans: We put our heart into the work.
How long will it take you?

meanings.note: Marks beneficiary (per i ragazzi), duration/target (quanto per Corinna?), or reason (scusa per prima).
Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).
Compound cardinal numeral (cento + settanta), naming a script scene.

examples.trans: Let us set up scene one seventy.
We are on page one seventy.

meanings.note: Imperative lascia! tells someone to back off or leave someone be.
Unstressed 1st-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun (mi sento, mi piace, mi serve).

meanings.en: to be needed by (servire a qualcuno)
meanings.note: Works like piacere: mi serve ('he/it is needed by me' -> 'I need him/it').
Modal verb followed directly by an infinitive.

examples.trans: I have to talk to you.

meanings.note: Written with an accent to distinguish it from reflexive/impersonal pronoun si.

examples.trans: Yes, I am coming right away.

meanings.note: Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Core verb used in many idioms: non fa niente, fare schifo, farsi la doccia, fare il bravo.
Negative pronoun; pairs with non before the verb (non vuoi niente, non fa niente).
Standard expression of gratitude in all registers.
Standard polite farewell suitable with both acquaintances and strangers.
